A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same concept-erasure study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP and classification results for adversarial, in-context and noise-based probes, together with concept-tracing experiments and appendix results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative and qualitative classifier-guided probing results in Table 4 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds steered latent probing: a trained, timestep-aware latent classifier supplies gradients during diffusion sampling, optionally combined with the noise-based probe. This introduces a substantial new component to the evaluation suite. The existing noise-probe formulation is retained; its expanded explanation does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix D.5.1 adds ImageNet-1k positive/negative datasets for training the latent classifiers, including other classes as negatives. Erasure evaluation retains the same ten object concepts and three art styles, without adding a broader application domain or erasure benchmark.

E2.justification: Standard classifier guidance becomes an evaluated reference for the combined classifier-guided noise probe in Table 4 and Figure 6. The existing erased-model comparator set—GA, UCE, ESD-x, ESD-u, Task Vector, STEREO and RECE—and earlier attack and sampler comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new classifier probe introduces a 90/10 training-validation split, noisy-timestep training and validation, and inference selection over 24 guidance strengths. Existing experimental settings largely persist. Section 3.3 changes noise-probe selection wording from highest CLIP score to highest CLIP/classification score, although Appendix D.3 still specifies CLIP alone; this implementation detail remains ambiguous.

E4.justification: The added latent-steering experiment tests whether classifier gradients recover concepts that resist other probes. Comparing classifier guidance with and without added noise tests their interaction, supported by Table 4 and the airliner examples in Figure 6. Existing sampler comparisons and dynamic concept tracing are retained, including the tracing plot moved to Appendix D.6.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C.3.4 specifies matched sets of 100 seeds per concept for inversion consistency; that disclosure is removed in v5. Existing standard-deviation tables and concept-tracing 95% confidence intervals are retained unchanged. The new classifier-guidance table adds no uncertainty estimates or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: All six matched numerical tables retain their values, including appendix means and standard deviations. New Table 4 reports substantial additional recovery results: STEREO classification accuracy is 5.8% with standard classifier guidance and 20.3% with classifier-guided noise probing; UCE reports 45.6% and 75.6%, respectively. These are newly reported probing conditions, not improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: v5 removes v1 Appendix B.1's partial-latent-retention and ODE/SDE assumptions, positive recovery-probability claim, and support-theorem proof sketch. The DDIM noise-probe equations remain. v5 also adds mathematical exposition of UCE's objective and conditional redirection, plus classifier-guidance equations and a Bayesian score decomposition.

C1.justification: The two conceptual mechanisms and the need for complementary evaluations remain central. The abstract and conclusion shift emphasis from the robustness–utility tradeoff and explaining a mechanistic dichotomy toward recovery beyond adversarial text, explicitly adding classifier guidance to the contribution. The conclusion presents mechanism categorization more cautiously as guidance for future research.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 explicitly makes mechanism assignments tentative and states that exact mechanistic conclusions require further study. Section 5 adds the substantive limitation that optimization may induce a concept the model never encountered, rather than reveal retained knowledge. Section 2 also develops UCE as a conditional-redirection example. These changes substantially qualify what successful probing establishes.

D1.justification: Appendix D.5 supplies extensive new classifier implementation information: dataset construction, preprocessing, VAE encoding, architecture, optimizer, class-weighted loss, noise augmentation and inference steering. Project and repository access addresses are updated, rather than code availability being newly introduced. The earlier inversion-consistency implementation paragraph is removed; existing erasure-training details largely remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds Dhariwal and Nichol for classifier guidance, Sharma et al. for related unlearning evaluation, and the DDIM reference. It removes the SDE and support-theorem references accompanying the deleted proof. In-context probing is no longer called a novel application and acknowledges additional prior work, while most related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, conceptual-model section, noise-probe explanation, dynamic-tracing interpretation, summary and conclusion are rewritten. The appendices gain a contents page and separate erasure implementation, probing methods and full results into distinct sections. This is extensive narrative and organizational revision beyond the added experiment.

P2.justification: v5 adds the classifier-guidance table and airliner figure, relocates the original concept-tracing plot from main-text Figure 5 to appendix Figure 9, and repositions other retained illustrations. It also enlarges the unrelated-concept examples and places both full-results tables together. Existing plots, image examples and overall visual design are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v5 adds a documented latent-guidance test with quantitative and visual evidence, while more explicitly acknowledging that recovered outputs need not prove retained knowledge. These improve diagnostic coverage and interpretation. The gains remain bounded: the original benchmark results are unchanged, the recovery proof sketch is removed, and the new Table 4 lacks uncertainty estimates. Overall, the empirical extension and more careful qualifications provide a limited net improvement.
